title: Let us praise the rod from Jesse

edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia, Latin column, In annuntiationem Sermo I, printed p. 14, col. A (PDF p. 38)

source_text: Venite igitur, dilectissimi, et nos ad memoriam, ea quae praecesserunt, revocantes, virgam illam ex Iesse sic admirabiliter atque ineffabiliter germinantem glorificemus, collaudemus, beatam praedicemus, laetisque acclamationibus excipiamus.
pass_a_gloss: Come (venite) therefore, most beloved, and we, recalling to memory the things which went before, that rod from Jesse (virga ex Iesse) so wonderfully and unspeakably sprouting (germinantem) let us glorify, let us praise together, let us proclaim blessed (beatam praedicemus), and with glad acclamations let us receive (excipiamus).

choices.choice: 'virgam ... ex Iesse ... germinantem' alludes to Isaiah 11:1; cited.
'beatam praedicemus' may echo Luke 1:48 ('all generations will call me blessed'); possible, not cited.

pass_b_english: Come then, dearly beloved, and let us too, calling to mind what has gone before, glorify that rod from Jesse that blossomed so wonderfully and beyond all telling (Isaiah 11:1). Let us praise it together, call it blessed, and welcome it with joyful acclamations.
notes: 'virgam ... ex Iesse ... germinantem' alludes to Isaiah 11:1; cited. 'beatam praedicemus' may echo Luke 1:48 ('all generations will call me blessed'); possible, not cited. The rod (virga, feminine) stands for Mary; 'it' keeps the image as the print has it.
